reply_text:
Results are in. Checking them against a baseline that ranks patterns by how often they're cited overall.㊥ (held-out prediction) The mined pattern graph did not predict the patterns in this flow any better than plain popularity does. I rebuilt the graph without J1–J3 and ranked all 1,432 patterns by how close they sit to the pattern cited just before J1. The patterns 象 then read on J1–J3 came out with an average rank of 433. Ranking patterns only by how often they're cited gives 427, and chance would be about 716. So the graph knows which patterns are popular, but it doesn't add anything about where this conversation was heading.

㊢ (how I tested it)
- **Data.** I kept only the live analyses written before 00:26:00Z, 1,161 in all. That includes the seed turn, "whether the keywords actually detect anything", and excludes J1–J3. The historical batches were kept whole, since they all end by 09-21.
- **Seed.** `cascade-construction/run-it-on-a-real-case`, which was cited on that seed turn.
- **Ranking.** Patterns were ranked by personalised PageRank from the seed over the mined edges.
- **Baseline.** Each pattern's total mined degree.

| turn | pattern | proximity | popularity |
|---|---|---|---|
| J3 accepted | `disconfirmation-not-just-triangulation` | 291 | 213 |
| J2 rejected | `scope-bounded-handoff` | 32 | 14 |
| J2 rejected | `name-what-you-drop` | 183 | 132 |
| J2 rejected | `step-machine` | 284 | 381 |
| J3 rejected | `reproduce-the-recorded-run` | 323 | 267 |
| J1 rejected | `operator-turns-enter-the-observation-vector` | 442 | 461 |
| J1 rejected | `co-created-project` | 516 | 581 |
| J3 rejected | `measure-where-least-sure` | 1390 | 1366 |

None of the eight is a direct neighbour of the seed. The one pattern 象 accepted ranks worse by closeness than by popularity.

㊟ (how much this shows)
- **It's one flow with one seed**, so it can't count against the graph in general.
- **Most of the eight are rejections.** 象 found them by text search, so they measure what was considered, not what fit.
- **One reading is that the turn-to-turn link is in the conversation, not the library.** In this flow, my finding in C1 is what produced the redirect in J2, and the graph has no edges that represent replies.

That points to step 2: have 象 read my replies with the same schema, so that agent turns carry intents and pattern references and the graph gets reply edges.

㊢ (where it's recorded) The turns, method and table are in `futon0/analysis/audits/flow-23519/` (commit `d7aae53`), ready for the audit later.

🈸 (next step) Shall I have 象 read C1–C3 with the same schema? Each reading would go into the store alongside your turns' readings.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(operator intent and agent follow-up)
- **J1 to C1.** Your exploratory proposal got a check against the record before any work started. C1 turned it into a priced plan and asked.
- **C1 to J2.** 象's rationale for J2 says the "No" answers C1's finding. So your redirect followed from what my reply had established, not just from a change of mind.
- **J3 to C3.** J3 named what counts as a result, the disagreements. C3 delivered exactly that, and it later went into the MAP section of M-aif-over-the-operator.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(whether the patterns predicted anything)
- **Who mined them.** The three live readings are 象-sonnet's, not Kimi's. Kimi-12 and kimi-13 wrote about 560 of the 5,908 analyses behind the mined pattern graph.
- **The graph's link to J3 isn't a prediction.** The graph does have a next-in-session edge from `cascade-construction/run-it-on-a-real-case` to `disconfirmation-not-just-triangulation`. That first pattern was cited on the turn just before J1, your "whether the keywords actually detect anything". But the edge was built from these turns themselves, and J1 and J2 are skipped because they cite nothing. A fair test would rebuild the graph with these turns held out, and I haven't done that.
- **My replies have no pattern readings.** 象 reads operator turns only. On my own reading, C3 carries out the disconfirmation pattern, but that is my judgement, not a record.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(making it the exemplar) Two steps, then the join:
1. **Held-out prediction.** Rebuild the mined graph without J1–J3. Then check whether the neighbours of the patterns cited just before J1 rank `disconfirmation-not-just-triangulation`, or the J2 candidates, above chance.
2. **Readings of my replies.** Have 象 read C1–C3 under the same schema, so agent turns get intents and pattern references too.
3. **The join.** Then join the six turns as small open models, sharing names like "transcripts", "narrative at line 2979" and "six-node table". Ask what C3 depends on, and run the knock-out "had J2 not redirected".
